tagline: Reservoir shores and a replacement road at the foot of the Smokies
intro: The Indian Lakes drive links Topton and Almond by US 129 and NC 28. NC 28’s Almond–Deals Gap section is a state scenic byway. The North Carolina Department of Transportation describes the overlapping Fontana Byway as a winding drive along Cheoah Lake at the base of the Great Smoky Mountains, highlighting lake views and the engineering of Fontana Dam. Fontana Lake has coves and islands formed from former mountain peaks; when water levels fall, its steep banks are exposed.

The Tennessee Valley Authority built Fontana Dam during World War II to meet electricity demand from the aluminum industry. Its reservoir submerged most of NC 288, the highway between Deals Gap and Bryson City. A surviving western section returned as NC 288 before new construction connected Fontana and Almond in 1954; the whole remaining NC 288 route then became NC 28.

From Topton, US 129 heads north through Robbinsville toward Deals Gap. At the US 129 junction, take NC 28 along Cheoah Lake toward Fontana. A side road leads across the dam. Continue toward Almond beside Fontana Lake’s southern shore, with Great Smoky Mountains National Park bordering the lake to the north. At Almond, the post office, school and railway depot were moved in 1943 during dam construction.

moments.title: Robbinsville
moments.text: The courthouse in the center of Robbinsville is the third to serve Graham County. The original courthouse was built in 1874. Two decades later, its floor gave way while the building was packed for a murder trial. A replacement followed in 1895, the last wooden courthouse built in North Carolina. The current building, completed in 1942, is a stone Classical Revival design by Barber and McMurry of Knoxville. Works Progress Administration funding helped build it during the Depression era. The T-shaped building stands at 12 North Main Street, in the center of the county seat.

moments.title: Deals Gap
moments.text: Deals Gap names both a mountain pass on the state line and a community 0.7 miles south of it, at US 129 and NC 28. Across the line in Tennessee, US 129 becomes the eleven-mile Tail of the Dragon, a destination for motorcycle and sports-car drivers. The two-lane road runs mostly through forest, with overlooks and places to pull off. The Dragon name has been used since 1981. Named bends include Copperhead Corner and Hog Pen Bend, two of the road’s sharp turns. Here the Fontana Byway begins at the junction, following NC 28 south.

moments.title: Fontana Dam
moments.text: The Appalachian Trail crosses the top of Fontana Dam, 480 feet above its base. The Tennessee Valley Authority began construction on January 1, 1942. Two generators began operating in January 1945, supplying electricity for wartime aluminum production. The reservoir required the relocation of 1,311 families, 1,047 graves and more than 60 miles of roads. Fontana, Bushnell, Forney and Judson were completely submerged. The dam takes its name from the lost lumber and copper-mining town at Eagle Creek. South of the dam, the workers’ village became Fontana Village, where some original 1940s buildings remain in use.
